title: Female borrowers who use generic business labels, such as 'sari-sari store', may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the specific goal of saving money to expand may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who specify their exact academic field of study may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the loan amount in local currency may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who describe social interest repayment through volunteering may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include direct thank you notes to lenders may fund more slowly.
Pitches from women that specify exact demographic figures, such as the number of children, relationship status, or husband's occupation, tend to decelerate funding speed.
Female borrowers who request higher loan amounts may fund faster than those requesting smaller amounts.
Mentioning benefits for children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention their general family structure fund faster.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayments predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Mentioning family obligations and benefits has opposite effects on funding speed by gender.
Female borrowers who provide specific details about family members or spouse employment fund faster.
